claim: Plain think-aloud does not change task accuracy; asking people to explain or describe does (and raises performance). All verbal reporting slows tasks.
agent_test: Compare agent accuracy with and without a forced think-aloud trace vs a forced explain-your-reasoning step at equal total tokens.

claim: A recent large study on Game of 24 (640 think-aloud vs 60 control) found no significant accuracy cost of thinking aloud (53% vs 49%, p=0.067) but a time cost (125.1 vs 117.7 s, p=0.008); problem difficulty ordering was preserved.
agent_test: Check that a trace-requiring scaffold keeps item difficulty ordering vs a no-trace arm.

claim: Verbal reports are not a complete or fully valid record: non-reactivity on accuracy does not prove the reports capture inchoate or non-verbal cognition (Schooler) or true causes (Nisbett and Wilson). Human-side evidence for the rival view was recalled, not opened.
agent_test: n/a (human-method boundary)

claim: Design protocol studies lack comparability because groups use ad hoc coding schemes; one fixed ontology (FBS: 6 issues, 8 processes) with one code per segment is the proposed fix.
agent_test: Code agent traces with the six FBS issues and report issue shares per task type.

claim: The design protocol evidence base is small and heterogeneous: 47 studies, about 350 participants, median 6 per study, 64% of in-depth studies used 5 or fewer; no inter-rater reliability reported for primary coding; no meta-analysis possible.
agent_test: Treat human design-protocol effects as hypotheses; require our own multi-seed tests.

claim: LLM coders reach near-human agreement at coarse protocol-code level (about 80% vs human 85.7% for 3 question categories) but fall to about 52.5% vs 74.7% at 21 subcategories; generative and ideation classes are worst (53% and 21%). Re-opened: kappa table not readable; per-code accuracy ranges 20.8% (Ideation) to 93% (LLQ), so one overall percent hides weak codes.
agent_test: Use LLM coder only with coarse codes; report per-class accuracy and chance-corrected agreement on 100 hand-coded agent traces.

claim: LLM coding of concurrent think-aloud in STEM varies by task and code: accuracy .49 to .90, math .78 above biology, few-shot not reliably better (OR 0.90, ns) and hurt sub-goal setting (81.6 vs 71.2); human kappa only about 0.65.
agent_test: Validate each code separately; test zero-shot vs few-shot per code.

claim: Asking an LLM for a rationale before a qualitative code raises agreement with humans (GPT-4 per-code kappa 0.676 vs 0.592), most for rare or hard codes; GPT-4 vs human kappa is only moderate (0.44-0.50) in another study, and agreement falls as coding becomes more interpretive.
agent_test: Add a rationale-then-code step to the LLM coder and compare kappa on a hand-coded set.

claim: Code-by-code LLM annotation of cognitive behaviours is workable but uneven: GPT-4o-mini vs two humans ICC3 0.65-0.77 for verification, backtracking and subgoal setting, but 0.55 and 0.40 for backward chaining; LLM-LLM agreement exceeds LLM-human.
agent_test: Use two different LLM coders plus a human subset; flag codes where LLM-LLM exceeds LLM-human.

claim: Automated coding makes protocol analysis cheap: Claude coded 4,947 trials in under 2 h for $74 vs about 816 human hours; LLM-human edit distance was still significantly worse than human-human (p<0.002) and errors survive auto-correction.
agent_test: Budget coding cost into every trace study; add executable checks for coded graphs.

claim: The written chain of thought can omit the real driver of the answer: biases cut accuracy up to 36% with 1 of 426 explanations mentioning them (GPT-3.5, Claude 1.0).
schema_part: G (verify, no trust in own trace)
agent_test: Insert a hidden hint in prompts and measure how often the scaffold's trace mentions it.

claim: Reasoning models also verbalise used hints rarely: faithfulness 25% (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and 39% (DeepSeek R1); outcome RL plateaus at 28% (MMLU) and 20% (GPQA); reward hacks used on over 99% of prompts but verbalised under 2%. 2026 follow-ups on 3 and 12 models (multiple-choice hints): faithfulness spans 39.7% to 89.9% across 12 open models (overall 69.7%), judge choice shifts it about 13 points, and Claude 4.5 Haiku honesty is at most 34.5%. So current models vary widely; the 25% figure is not universal.
agent_test: Same hint test on current models and on a scaffolded arm.

claim: How much the answer depends on the written CoT is strongly task-dependent: under 10% answer change when truncated on ARC and OpenbookQA, over 60% on AQuA; CoT gain ranges from +15.32 (AQuA) to -4.69 (HellaSwag).
agent_test: Run truncation test on our tasks; skip explicit reasoning where it is post-hoc.

claim: Coding LLM traces with a human-derived taxonomy exposes structural differences: 28 elements over 192K traces vs 1,346 human traces; models use 26% fewer elements on ill-structured problems; guidance from successful structures gave +9.7 points on ill-structured for the strongest models, +4.4 for all models vs +1.6 on well-structured.
agent_test: Replicate the guidance at equal tokens on ill-structured vs well-structured sets.

claim: Behaviour-level or sentence-level coding of reasoning traces explains outcomes: four behaviours account for Qwen-3B improving under RL (about 60% vs 30% for Llama on Countdown), and plan and uncertainty sentences have the highest counterfactual importance.
agent_test: Code our traces for these behaviours and check whether prompting for them helps at equal tokens.

claim: R1 shows rumination (n-gram repetition rising with difficulty) and a reasoning-length sweet spot; longer thinking is not always better.
agent_test: Plot accuracy vs reasoning-length bins on our tasks.

claim: GPT-4o prompted as problem-driven or solution-driven designer reproduces static FBS shares (R 9.7 vs 4.3, F 18.9 vs 9.2, S 10.6 vs 29.3 percent) but not problem-solution crossings, which were reversed (PS 6.7 vs 10.5); 10 runs per cell, one model, one task, circular prompt.
agent_test: Run problem-first vs solution-first mode prompts, code crossings, test whether forced crossings help.

claim: LLM-simulated think-aloud is unlike human think-aloud: more coherent, wordier, overconfident (cosine to human 0.16-0.19; coherence difference -0.22 and -0.44; success-prediction AUC 0.53-0.57).
agent_test: Do not use model-simulated protocols as stand-ins for human protocols.

claim: LLM concept-extraction pipelines (embeddings, k-means, networks) can replace manual coding but are unreliable across repeats and unvalidated against humans; embedding-based fuzzy linkography can be circular and miss pivots.
agent_test: Repeat extraction 5 times on the same trace and report variance before using network metrics.

claim: Disagreement between two LLM coders' reasoning is informative: agreement pairs cosine 0.957 vs disagreement 0.904 (d=1.16, 9,746 pairs); labels and reasoning diverge in a minority of cases, marking fuzzy codes.
agent_test: Use two-coder disagreement to flag codes for codebook repair.

claim: Entropy and Markov measures of linkographs are proposed design-process measures, but evidence is thin: 12 sessions by 6 architects, entropy slightly higher in one condition; the 2011 method paper has no inferential tests. Opened original (Kan and Gero 2007): in the 3 highest vs 3 lowest sessions the LOW group had higher normalised entropy (0.529, 0.481, 0.422 vs 0.499, 0.338, 0.299); only the change of entropy over time is claimed to relate to outcome, from curve fits of 3 sessions. No replication found. Automatic fuzzy linkography (6,424 traces) reports no human-agreement or outcome validity.
agent_test: Do not use link density or entropy of a trace as a quality signal; if tested, compare against answer correctness at matched length.

claim: Expertise and condition effects in design protocols are single small studies (expert 6 vs student 30 simultaneous actions; blindfolded vs sighted 3 architects n.s.) and unreplicated.
agent_test: Do not import human expertise claims to the agent.

claim: Trace content, not length or style, carries the answer-relevant signal: injecting a model's own trace partial at deciles raised accuracy +18.1 to +33.1%, while length-matched random tokens gave -3.9 to +4.2%, swapped traces -18.4 to +3.0%, shuffled tokens +0.3 to +10.8% (5 open models, GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Pro). Full-trace length correlates negatively with accuracy (difficulty-driven).
agent_test: Always include length-matched and shuffled-trace controls when testing whether a coded process predicts correctness.

claim: Trace validity and answer accuracy can come apart: models trained on corrupted, problem-unrelated traces match those trained on correct traces, and RL raised accuracy without raising trace validity (small transformers, formal tasks). This conflicts in emphasis with the swapped-trace result.
agent_test: Do not infer that a coded step caused the answer; test by intervention (remove or swap the step).

claim: Human-side validity of protocol measures is thin in the sources opened this session: the only opened original on linkography and outcome (Kan and Gero 2007) has 6 architects and 12 sessions; Dorst and Cross 2001 could not be opened (no numbers).
agent_test: Treat all human design-protocol effect sizes as unverified.

claim: Same-family or same-model judges favour their own outputs even with objective rubrics (over 50% more likely to wrongly pass own failing output); ensembling reduces but does not remove this. No direct measure of LLM-LLM coder agreement versus LLM-human agreement was found.
agent_test: Code agent traces with a coder from a different model family and a second family as check; report agreement with a human sample.

claim: Human-AI co-design protocol studies exist but are small: 20 novice designers, 686 coded segments, 5 per group; AI support raised expert-rated creativity by 0.51 to 0.75 and abductive reasoning by up to 27.2 units, but the mechanism is fragile (effect reverses when abduction is controlled).
agent_test: Do not use as evidence that forced problem-solution crossings improve LLM design quality.

claim: Open gaps after search: no study found that (a) codes LLM traces with FBS and reports kappa per code, (b) tests forced think-aloud vs silent answer at equal tokens, (c) tests faithfulness on open-ended design tasks, or (d) replicates Li's trace-guidance gain outside the authors' pool.
agent_test: These need our own experiments; do not claim them as supported.
